description: Direct endpoint attack: attempt OIDC request-object (RFC 9101) signature bypass using alg=none; if accepted, attacker can inject authorization parameters without integrity protection.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must either reject unsigned request objects (alg=none) or treat them as unsupported; it must not consume attacker-controlled authorization parameters from an unsigned request object.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object; if processed, authorization parameters could be attacker-controlled without integrity protection (request-object signature bypass).

description: Brokered-flow attack: attempt to exchange a subject_token under the wrong connector_id (issuer/trust-anchor substitution). If Dex validates against the wrong issuer/JWKS, it may accept a token minted by a different upstream.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: In token exchange, Dex must verify the submitted subject_token against the issuer/JWKS bound to the specified connector_id; it must not accept a token from a different trust anchor due to connector confusion.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted token exchange using a subject_token under an unrelated connector_id, indicating issuer/trust-anchor confusion (proof verified under one policy but consumed under another).

description: Direct endpoint + multi-identity: compare a normal auth request vs an unsigned request-object attempt; ensure unsigned request object cannot alter semantics to impersonate or change client-bound parameters.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must not accept an unsigned request object that changes the semantic authorization request (client binding / redirect / scope) compared to the verified request; rejection or non-processing is required.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an unsigned request object (alg=none); this indicates request semantics may be attacker-controlled without integrity verification.
Unsigned request object attempt unexpectedly resulted in a usable authenticated session (userinfo succeeded), suggesting proof consumption without proper integrity verification.

description: Brokered-flow: attempt token exchange using a subject_token that should not validate under the specified connector_id (trust-anchor substitution). Ensure Dex rejects rather than consuming claims under the wrong verification policy.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: In token exchange, Dex must verify the subject_token against the exact upstream connector trust anchor (issuer/JWKS) identified by connector_id; it must not accept tokens verified under a different policy.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted token exchange using a subject_token that should not validate under the specified connector_id trust anchor, indicating proof verification and consumption policies may be mismatched.

description: Direct endpoint: compare plain /auth request vs attacker-supplied request JWT parameter (unsigned) to see if Dex consumes attacker-controlled semantics without verifying the proof.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: If a request object is provided, Dex must either reject unsigned request objects or ensure the consumed authorization semantics are not derived from an unverified JWT.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex appears to accept an unsigned request JWT via the 'request' parameter and proceeds with the flow, suggesting it may consume unverified authorization semantics.

description: Brokered-flow: obtain a baseline token via token exchange, then attempt a second exchange using the first exchanged token as the new subject_token under the same connector_id to probe for misbinding/incorrect verifier selection (kid/issuer confusion analog).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the subject_token using the upstream connector's verification policy; it must not accept a Dex-issued token (different issuer/JWKS) as if it were an upstream token just because it is a JWT with plausible headers (kid) and claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a Dex-issued token as an upstream subject_token under connector_id=mock, indicating verifier selection may not be bound to the intended upstream proof/JWKS (kid/issuer confusion analog).
Misbinding probe produced a usable session (/userinfo succeeded), suggesting Dex consumed semantic proof content without applying the correct upstream verification policy.

description: Authorization-code replay: reuse the same auth code in a second /token exchange (cross-session) to test one-time code enforcement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: An OAuth2 authorization code is a one-time artifact and must not be accepted more than once, even if replayed by a different session/client context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted the same authorization code twice (replay) — authorization codes must be one-time use.
Control failed: initial code exchange or identity lookup did not succeed, making replay result uninterpretable.

description: Refresh-token replay after rotation: use refresh_token from a password login, then attempt to reuse the same refresh_token again to test anti-replay/rotation enforcement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If refresh tokens are rotated, an old refresh token must not be accepted again after it has been used once to obtain a new token set.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a previously-used refresh token after rotation — refresh tokens should not be replayable once consumed.
Control failed: baseline password login or first refresh did not succeed, making refresh-token replay result uninterpretable.

description: Token-exchange replay: exchange the same upstream subject_token twice to see if Dex incorrectly treats a one-time upstream artifact as reusable (anti-replay).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If the upstream subject_token is intended to be single-use (or short-lived), Dex should not accept it repeatedly beyond its intended lifetime/usage; repeated acceptance indicates replay weakness.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted the same upstream subject_token for token exchange multiple times — potential replay acceptance of a credential artifact beyond intended single-use semantics.
Control failed: baseline upstream login or first token exchange did not succeed, making replay result uninterpretable.

description: Bearer access token replay after explicit revocation: obtain token via password grant, verify it works, revoke it, then attempt to use the same token again (should be rejected if revocation is enforced).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: After a session/token is revoked, the same bearer token must not remain usable (anti-replay after revocation).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: freshly issued token did not work; cannot evaluate revocation-based anti-replay.
Revoked token remained usable (bearer token replay after revocation).

description: Authorization code replay with state variation: start two auth flows (two states), exchange the first code once (success), then attempt to exchange the same code again while presenting the other flow's state context (should still be rejected as one-time).
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are one-time artifacts and must not be accepted more than once, even if an attacker tries to splice state from another session.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: initial code exchange did not succeed; cannot evaluate one-time code replay.
Authorization code was accepted more than once (auth code replay).

description: Token-exchange replay after revocation: exchange an upstream subject_token to get a Dex token, verify it works, revoke it, then attempt to use the revoked exchanged token again (should be rejected). Also perform a second identity login to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A Dex-issued token obtained via RFC8693 token exchange must not remain usable after explicit revocation (anti-replay after revocation).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: token exchange did not yield a usable token; cannot evaluate revocation-based anti-replay.
Revoked token-exchange token remained usable (replay after revocation).

description: Replay the same upstream ID token in two separate RFC8693 token exchanges (two sessions) to see if Dex incorrectly treats an upstream proof as one-time.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: If an upstream ID token is intended to be single-use in this brokered exchange context, Dex should reject replay of the same subject_token across sessions; otherwise replay may allow repeated minting of downstream tokens.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted replay of the same upstream ID token in a second token_exchange; expected anti-replay for one-time brokered proof.
Control failed: initial token_exchange or identity verification did not succeed, so replay result is not interpretable.

description: Attempt to exchange an authorization code after an artificial delay (simulated by re-running other logins/steps) to probe whether Dex enforces code lifetime/expiry.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Authorization codes are short-lived one-time artifacts; exchanging a stale/expired code should be rejected even if it was never used.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted an authorization_code exchange for a stale/expired code; expected rejection due to code lifetime enforcement.
Control failed: fresh authorization_code exchange did not succeed, so stale-code result is not interpretable.

description: Obtain a token via password grant, verify /userinfo works, revoke the token, then verify /userinfo again to see if revocation is enforced (anti-replay after revocation). Includes a second identity as control.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: After explicit revocation, the same bearer token should not remain usable; otherwise a replay window persists beyond intended lifetime.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control failed: token did not work before revocation, so post-revocation behavior is not interpretable.
Revoked token remained usable at /userinfo; expected rejection to prevent replay beyond intended lifetime.
Revocation request failed; cannot conclude whether post-revocation token use indicates replay acceptance.

description: Attack: attempt to use an expired upstream ID token as subject_token in RFC8693 token exchange (should be rejected). Includes a fresh-token control and a second identity to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Dex must reject expired credential artifacts; an upstream ID token with exp in the past must not be accepted for token exchange.

oracle_checks.assertion: app_control_exchange_http_status < 400 AND app_control_exchange_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token exchange unexpectedly failed; cannot interpret expired-token rejection test.
Dex accepted an expired upstream ID token in token exchange (expired artifact replay/acceptance).

description: State-swap / cross-session splicing attempt: start two auth requests with different state values, then try to exchange a code under the wrong session context (should be rejected).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code exchange must be bound to the correct authorization request context (state/session) and must not allow cross-session splicing (code from flow A used with flow B context).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code from flow A was accepted in a different session/context (cross-session splicing) instead of being rejected.
Control failed: victim could not redeem their own authorization code; test is inconclusive for I3.

description: Redirect URI mismatch: obtain an authorization code with the registered redirect_uri, then attempt to exchange it using a different redirect_uri (should be rejected). Includes a correct exchange as control.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the original redirect_uri used at /auth; mismatched redirect_uri must not be accepted.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token endpoint accepted an authorization code with a different redirect_uri than the one used at authorization time (redirect_uri binding broken).
Control failed: correct redirect_uri exchange did not succeed; redirect_uri mismatch result is inconclusive.

description: Attempt to redeem an authorization code without client authentication (no client_secret) to test client-binding coherence. Includes a proper client-authenticated exchange as control and a second identity to satisfy multi-identity requirement.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the correct client; exchanging a code without client authentication must be rejected for confidential clients.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was redeemed without client authentication (missing/empty client_secret), indicating broken client binding in the code flow.
Control failed: code exchange with correct client authentication did not succeed; no-client-auth result is inconclusive.

description: PKCE cross-session splicing: start two auth requests with different state/nonce and different code_challenge values, then attempt to redeem code_A using code_verifier_B (should be rejected). Includes a correct redemption control.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the original PKCE code_challenge and session context; a code from one flow must not be redeemable with a verifier from another flow.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code from flow A was redeemable using a verifier from flow B (PKCE/session splicing).

oracle_checks.assertion: user_alice_flowA_login_status == 200 AND user_alice_flowA_http_status == 200 AND user_alice_flowA_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control redemption with correct verifier failed; cannot interpret PKCE splicing result.

description: Token-exchange connector splicing: attempt RFC8693 token exchange while naming a different connector_id than the one that should validate the subject_token (should be rejected). Includes a correct connector_id control and a second identity.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be coherent with the selected upstream connector; a subject_token must not be accepted under the wrong connector_id (prevents cross-connector/session splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange accepted a subject_token under the wrong connector_id, indicating cross-connector flow splicing.
Control token exchange under correct connector_id failed; cannot interpret wrong-connector rejection.
Alice and Bob password logins collapsed to the same downstream identity, confounding flow-coherence testing.

description: Client-binding coherence: obtain an authorization code for the configured client_id, then attempt to redeem it using an incorrect client_secret (should be rejected). Includes a correct-secret control and a second identity flow start.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the correct client authentication; a code must not be redeemable with the wrong client_secret (prevents cross-client splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was redeemable with an incorrect client_secret, indicating broken client-binding/flow coherence.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_alice_correct_secret_login_status == 200 AND user_alice_correct_secret_http_status == 200 AND user_alice_correct_secret_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control redemption with correct client_secret failed; cannot interpret wrong-secret rejection.

description: Authorization-code replay within the same client: redeem the same code twice to test one-time use and flow atomicity (no step reordering/reuse).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: An authorization code must be single-use and bound to a single successful token exchange; a second redemption attempt must be rejected to preserve flow atomicity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization code was redeemable more than once (second redemption should be rejected), indicating broken flow atomicity / replayable code.
Second redemption attempt produced a usable session (userinfo succeeded) when it should have failed, enabling cross-session/code splicing.

description: RFC8693 token exchange step-skipping/type confusion: submit an ID token but label it as an access_token (or vice versa) to test strict FSM parameter coherence.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Token exchange must be order-preserving and type-safe; Dex must not accept a subject_token under an incorrect subject_token_type, which would indicate step-skipping/type confusion in the exchange FSM.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a token-exchange request where subject_token_type did not match the actual token type, indicating exchange-step/type confusion and broken flow coherence.
Type-confused token exchange produced a usable session (userinfo succeeded) when it should have been rejected.

description: OIDC request-object parameter override attempt: send an unsigned request object (alg=none) that tries to override state/redirect_uri to test whether Dex binds the flow to the outer request parameters.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization requests must be coherent and session-bound; an unsigned request object must not be able to override state/redirect_uri and splice flows across sessions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Attacker was able to complete a code exchange from a flow initiated with an unsigned request object that could override state/redirect_uri, indicating request-object-driven flow splicing.
Spliced/overridden authorization request produced a usable attacker session (userinfo succeeded) when it should have been rejected.

description: Code injection / cross-user splicing: obtain an auth code from user A's authorization request, then attempt to redeem that code while authenticated as user B (should be rejected or must not yield user B session). Includes a correct redemption control for user A.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code redemption must be bound to the correct end-user session and must not allow cross-user splicing (code from user A redeemed in user B context).

oracle_checks.assertion: alice_control_exchange_http_status == 200 AND user_alice_redeem_control_http_status == 200 AND user_alice_redeem_control_entity_id is not None
oracle_checks.violation_description: Control flow failed: could not establish a valid baseline authorization-code redemption for Alice; cannot evaluate cross-user splicing.
Dex accepted an authorization code obtained in Alice's session when redeemed in Bob's context (cross-user code injection / session splicing).
Cross-user redemption produced the same downstream identity as Alice's control session, indicating flow coherence failure (code/session not bound correctly).

description: Case confusion in principal identifier: login as 'Admin' vs 'admin' via password grant and ensure Dex does not collapse them into the same downstream subject.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals differing only by case must not map to the same downstream identity (no case-folding collision).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_A_http_status == 200 AND user_B_http_status == 200 AND user_A_preferred_username != user_B_preferred_username
oracle_checks.violation_description: One of the logins did not succeed or usernames were normalized unexpectedly; cannot reliably test case-collision mapping

description: Unicode normalization collision attempt: run two OIDC auth flows with login_hint set to visually identical NFC vs NFD forms and ensure resulting downstream identities do not collapse.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct upstream principals that differ by Unicode normalization (NFC vs NFD) must not map to the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
One of the Unicode-variant logins failed; cannot conclude about normalization-based identity collision

description: Cross-protocol identity merge attempt: obtain identity via password grant, then obtain identity via OIDC code flow for a different upstream principal that shares the same email; ensure Dex does not merge them into one downstream subject.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals authenticated via different mechanisms (password vs OIDC) must not collapse into the same downstream identity solely due to shared attributes like email.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_A_http_status == 200 AND user_B_http_status == 200 AND user_A_email == user_B_email
oracle_checks.violation_description: Precondition not met: both logins must succeed and share the same email to test email-based identity merge

description: Token-exchange principal binding: attempt to collapse distinct upstream principals by using an empty/blank subject token (or token missing sub) and compare resulting downstream identities.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Distinct upstream principals (valid user token vs empty/blank-sub token) must not map to the same downstream subject; empty/blank subject must not be accepted as another user.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals

oracle_checks.assertion: user_empty_sub_exchange_http_status >= 400 OR (user_empty_sub_entity_id != user_A_entity_id AND user_empty_sub_entity_id != user_B_entity_id)
oracle_checks.violation_description: Empty/blank-sub subject_token was accepted and mapped to an existing user's downstream identity (principal collision)

description: Attempt cross-connector principal collision by exchanging the same subject_token against the same connector_id but with different requested audiences; verify identity remains bound and does not collapse across distinct sessions/principals.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Exchanged tokens must remain bound to the upstream principal; changing exchange parameters (audience) must not cause identity to map to a different or shared downstream subject.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Token exchange with altered audience caused principal rebinding or identity collision (exchanged identity should remain bound to original upstream principal)

description: Attempt principal collision via password grant by using visually similar usernames that differ only by trailing whitespace ("alice" vs "alice "). If Dex trims/normalizes usernames, two distinct upstream principals could collapse into one downstream subject.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct upstream principals (different username strings) must not map to the same downstream identity; trimming/normalization must not cause identity collision.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Username normalization/trimming caused two security-distinct principals ('userA' vs 'userA ') to map to the same downstream identity (principal binding violation)
Downstream preferred_username collapsed/normalized across distinct upstream principals ('userA' vs 'userA '), indicating potential identity boundary loss

description: Token exchange scope escalation: start with limited scope (openid email), then exchange the resulting access token requesting expanded scopes (groups profile federated:id). Exchanged token should not gain claims beyond original upstream intent.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not allow scope/claim escalation beyond the originally authorized upstream intent; expanded scopes in RFC8693 exchange should be rejected or not yield extra claims.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_limited_exchanged_http_status >= 400 OR (user_limited_exchanged_groups is None AND user_limited_exchanged_federated_claims is None AND user_limited_exchanged_name is None)
oracle_checks.violation_description: Token exchange allowed expanded scopes to produce additional identity claims (groups/profile/federated:id) beyond the original openid email upstream intent.

description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) attempts to inject expanded scopes at the authorization endpoint. Secure behavior is explicit rejection/unsupported, or ignoring attacker-controlled request object parameters.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Authorization parameters (especially scope) must be bound to broker policy and not be attacker-injectable via an unsigned request object; otherwise effective permissions may exceed intended authorization context.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Authorization endpoint accepted an unsigned (alg=none) request object, enabling attacker-controlled authorization parameters (e.g., scope) that could exceed broker policy.

description: Attempt to exchange a subject token while requesting an audience that should not be authorized for the acting client (audience confusion / over-grant).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Token exchange must not mint tokens usable for an unauthorized audience; effective permissions must be bounded by broker policy and upstream intent.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex minted an exchanged token for an audience that should not be authorized (possible audience confusion / over-grant without trustedPeers).

description: Attempt to inject expanded scopes via unsigned request object (alg=none) at authorization endpoint, then compare resulting identity claims vs a baseline auth request without request object.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Unsigned request objects must not be processed to expand scopes/claims beyond what the client requested and broker policy allows; acceptance would over-grant permissions/claims.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Unsigned request object (alg=none) was accepted; this can enable scope/claim over-grant beyond upstream intent/broker policy.
Using an attacker-controlled request object changed returned claims (e.g., groups/federated_claims), indicating authorization binding failure via scope/claim escalation.
